Date: 2026-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM); Ruth Delaney (Sable Head of Security), Marcus Chen (CTO), Anita Rao (Compliance), Leo Park (SRE)
summary: Tabletop-style security and availability review focusing on incident response, BCDR targets (RTO/RPO), SLA expectations and escalation paths. Sable emphasized EU data residency and HSM-backed KMS. Action items: share SOC2/ISO artifacts, provide runbook examples, schedule a drill.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a tabletop for resilience and compliance, try to keep this to about 50 minutes. Ruth, Marcus — thanks for making time.
[00:12] Ruth Delaney: Thanks Maya. quick context — Sable has a hard requirement for EU data residency for any PII and finance logs, and we need to understand your incident flow, like RTO and RPO when you failover between regions.
[00:26] Marcus Chen: also, we're evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted, mostly worried about keys, KMS, HSM support and auditability.
[00:35] Ethan Cole: great — I'll start with a brief on our incident lifecycle, then we can run a scenario. Redwood's incident response is tiered: detection -> triage -> mitigate -> restore -> root cause. We integrate with PagerDuty for on-call, and have SLA-backed runbooks for Dedicated customers.
[00:52] Leo Park: quick q — are logs exported to customer's SIEM automatically or is that an opt-in?
[00:57] Jordan Li: opt-in currently; we support streaming audit logs to customer endpoints — S3, syslog, or via our secure connector. retention policies are configurable per org, default 90 days for audit events.
[01:10] Ruth Delaney: 90 days is okay but we need fedramp-style retention for certain audits, we may need 7 years for specific records. Can you support longer retention and legal holds?
[01:22] Ethan Cole: yes, we can extend retention; for Hosted we store logs encrypted at rest and can push to customer-controlled buckets for longer retention. For Private and Dedicated, customers control the storage lifecycle. legal hold workflows we can support via export and immutability flags — we'll share details.
[01:38] Marcus Chen: KMS — what's the BYOK story? we require customer-managed keys in HSM for production.
[01:45] Maya Patel: short answer: supported. Redwood Private supports customer KMS integration (KMS or HSM) with key rotation policies and audit logging of key usage. For Hosted we offer a customer-managed KMS option for enterprise tiers.
[01:58] Ruth Delaney: is key usage logged per-request? we need per-token audit trails for access to sensitive models.
[02:05] Ethan Cole: yes, key operations and decryption events are logged. caveat: some internal transient caches (KV cache) may hold plaintext in memory for performance; access to that memory is restricted to the runtime and is never written to logs. we'll include a memory-handling note in the runbook.
[02:25] Marcus Chen: RTO/RPO — what numbers do you typically hit for Dedicated clusters in EU region? our current target is RTO <= 15 minutes and RPO <= 1 hour for inference endpoints serving latency-sensitive features.
[02:39] Ethan Cole: for Dedicated with auto-failover enabled we've seen effective RTOs around 5–12 minutes in controlled failovers; RPO depends on cache strategies — if prefix/KV caching is enabled, RPO can be sub-minute for stored state, but for burst requests it depends. for hosted, cross-region failover is usually 10–30 minutes.
[02:58] Leo Park: can you explain the fallback behavior? like if EU cluster goes down, do requests go to US and what about data residency?
[03:07] Ethan Cole: policy-based routing — we can configure strict-residency mode which blocks cross-region fallback, or soft-residency mode that fails over to a compatible region with prior approval and data processing addendum. Many enterprises choose soft mode for higher availability with explicit consent.
[03:24] Ruth Delaney: for Sable we need strict residency for PII; during the tabletop we want to see both strict and soft flows.
[03:30] Maya Patel: noted. we'll cover both scenarios.
[03:35] Ethan Cole: moving to SLAs — Redwood offers 99.95% for Dedicated (region-level) and our incident process includes credits for sustained degradations. community-hosted tiers are lower. The SLA includes escalation times: P1 -> 15 min ack, P2 -> 1 hour, etc.
[03:52] Marcus Chen: what's your on-call escalation chain? we need names/roles and that they're reachable 24/7 for P1s.
[03:59] Jordan Li: standard chain: customer's SRE raises ticket -> Redwood support triage -> on-call SE (PagerDuty) -> AE + engineering runbook -> senior engineering if needed. we'll supply an escalation matrix with phone/pager roles for pilot customers.
[04:16] Ruth Delaney: do you do tabletop drills with customers? we want an annual or semi-annual drill and a postmortem template that maps to SOC2 controls.
[04:24] Maya Patel: yes, we run tabletop drills and will co-facilitate. postmortem templates and evidence mapping to SOC2/ISO controls are part of our enterprise onboarding.
[04:34] Marcus Chen: scenario: EU region network partition at 15:00, control plane healthy but some worker nodes fail. describe the mitigation steps and customer-visible impacts.
[04:46] Ethan Cole: step 1: auto-detection via health checks triggers failover policy; step 2: Router tries local retry & if unavailable applies routing policy. If strict-residency is on, requests fail with HTTP 451/429 depending; if soft-residency, we route to fallback region with obfuscated telemetry to ensure no PII is transferred unless consented. step 3: engineering auto-scaling attempts to replace workers, if unsuccessful an on-call SE runs manual remediation — scale up replacement nodes, or activate warm standby in another AZ.
[05:14] Leo Park: warm standby — how long to warm up models? cold-starts can take several minutes due to weights loading.
[05:22] Ethan Cole: warm standby can keep the model loaded in memory (idle) for sub-30s response to first request, but cost goes up. typically the tradeoff is kept in the autoscaling policy; we can pin critical models in dedicated nodes to avoid cold start.
[05:36] Ruth Delaney: ok, for compliance we need documented RTO/RPO and a test plan. we'd like a 15-min RTO and 1-hour RPO for our production endpoints. can you commit to that on Dedicated?
[05:48] Ethan Cole: we can define those as contractual SLAs on Dedicated with runbook-driven failover and warm standby. We'll propose it in the Dedicated pricing/SLA deck.
[05:57] Marcus Chen: audit logs — what's the granularity? per-request, model version, prompt hash? we need to correlate calls back to user IDs for forensics.
[06:07] Ethan Cole: we log request metadata (timestamps, model, route, ttf, response codes) and we can include a prompt-hash and customer-provided identifiers. We avoid storing full PII in logs by default, but we can configure PII redaction or enrichment depending on the contract.
[06:24] Anita Rao: how do you handle legal holds and subpoena preservation?
[06:28] Jordan Li: we support exports to customer-controlled storage with immutability flags; for hosted customers we can export snapshots on request and we have process to preserve evidence while we investigate.
[06:38] Ruth Delaney: service continuity — what's your incident comms cadence? we require initial ack in 15 minutes and updates every 30 minutes for P1 until resolution.
[06:47] Maya Patel: standard P1 cadence is ack in 15 minutes, updates every 30 minutes, final postmortem within 7 business days. we'll include SLA terms in the contract.
[06:58] Marcus Chen: who signs the postmortem? we want executive-level confirmation.
[07:02] Maya Patel: postmortems include technical RCA and an exec summary; we provide a sign-off from our SRE lead and an assigned customer success sponsor.
[07:10] Leo Park: network partitions aside — what about a compromised API key incident? what's the containment plan?
[07:15] Ethan Cole: immediate step: revoke compromised key, rotate keys, invalidate active sessions, and if necessary rotate model access keys. We can force revocation customer-side via the console or API. Forensics: ingest logs into an isolated workspace and provide a timeline. We recommend short-lived credentials and role-based tokens for mitigation.
[07:36] Ruth Delaney: SSO — any limitations on SAML attributes mapping? we need groups to map to RBAC roles.
[07:42] Ethan Cole: we support SAML and SCIM for group sync. RBAC supports role hierarchy and custom roles. We'll share example mappings.
[07:52] Marcus Chen: encryption in transit? TLS 1.2+ and mTLS for private peering?
[07:58] Ethan Cole: yes TLS 1.2+ and we support mTLS for private links and VPC peering. For inter-service traffic inside the cluster we use mutual TLS as well.
[08:06] Jordan Li: want to flag something — there are a few tradeoffs: strict residency increases RTO risk; warm standby reduces RTO but increases cost; BYOK increases control but adds rotation/ops overhead for customer.
[08:18] Ruth Delaney: understood. for our procurement we need a runbook and a sample incident escalation matrix. Also SOC2 attestation and ISO 27001 evidence.
[08:27] Maya Patel: we'll bundle SOC2 Type II report, ISO cert link, and our incident runbook. Also proposing a tabletop drill on 2026-07-02.
[08:35] Marcus Chen: can we see a sample postmortem that maps findings to control families?
[08:39] Ethan Cole: yes — we'll provide a mapping doc that ties our incident steps to SOC2 CC and ISO Annex A controls.
[08:47] Anita Rao: one more question — do you offer contractual data residency guarantees with financial penalties?
[08:53] Maya Patel: yes, for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can include residency guarantees and SLA credits for breaches; specifics in legal addendum.
[09:02] Ruth Delaney: okay wrap up: we'd like an initial tabletop, your runbook, SOC/ISO docs, and a proposed Dedicated configuration and pricing.
[09:12] Maya Patel: perfect — we'll send items in the next 48 hours. Ethan, Jordan — anything to add?
[09:18] Ethan Cole: I'll craft the sample runbook and include failover playbooks for strict vs soft residency, plus warm standby guidance.
[09:26] Jordan Li: I'll open the pilot ticket and propose Dedicated cluster sizing based on your throughput numbers; Marcus, please send QPS and model sizes.
[09:34] Marcus Chen: will do.
[09:38] Maya Patel: thanks all. ending notes: follow-up email with attachments and proposed dates.
[09:45] --- end of recorded transcript (approx 52 minutes) ---

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings around product names (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache"). Some timestamps approximate.
